title: Projection-formula arrows
statement:
Work with sites small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $h:(\mathcal T,S)\to(\mathcal S,R)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi: an adjunction $h^{-1}\dashv h_*$ with $h^{-1}$ preserving finite limits, together with a map of sheaves of commutative rings $h^{-1}R\to S$. Module pullback is $h^*M=S\otimes_{h^{-1}R}h^{-1}M$, left adjoint to module direct image $h_*$. Use the unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], derived tensor and $Lh^*$ computed by K-flat resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and $Rh_*$ computed by K-injective resolutions [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist, lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. The derived adjunction $Lh^*\dashv Rh_*$ is the canonical one obtained from the ordinary module adjunction by [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general]; write $\varepsilon_E:Lh^*Rh_*E\to E$ for its counit.

Let $E\in D(S)$ and let $F^\bullet$ be a bounded complex of $R$-module sheaves with a strict-perfect package [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package], namely maps $i_r:F^r\to R^{\oplus N_r}$ and $p_r:R^{\oplus N_r}\to F^r$ with $p_ri_r=1$ and $N_r\in\mathbf N$. Define
$$
\pi_{h,E,F}:Rh_*E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F^\bullet
\longrightarrow Rh_*(E\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}Lh^*F^\bullet)
$$
to be the adjunct of
$$
Lh^*(Rh_*E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F^\bullet)
\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*Rh_*E\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}Lh^*F^\bullet
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_E\otimes1}E\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}Lh^*F^\bullet.
$$
Here the first arrow is the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].

For a free coefficient term $R^{\oplus N}$ in degree zero, let $\rho_N$ be the inverse of the finite-sum identification
$$
(Rh_*E)^{\oplus N}\xrightarrow{\pi_N}Rh_*(E^{\oplus N}).
$$
Finite sums here are finite products in the additive derived categories, and the right adjoint preserves them [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits]. For a package term define the derived morphism
$$
\rho_{F^r}=(1_{Rh_*E}\otimes p_r)\circ\rho_{N_r}\circ Rh_*(1_E\otimes h^*i_r).
$$
The tensor symbols in this display are derived tensor; the sheaves $F^r$ and $h^*F^r$ are flat retracts of finite free sheaves, so their ordinary pullbacks and tensor products compute these operations.

The following specifies the chain representatives used for bounded totalization. Fix a K-injective representative $I^\bullet$ of $E$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and put
$$
A=h_*I^\bullet,\qquad
C=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R F^\bullet),\qquad
J=\operatorname{Tot}(I^\bullet\otimes_S h^*F^\bullet),\qquad B=h_*J.
$$
Use the tensor total complexes of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], with differential $d_I\otimes1+(-1)^a1\otimes d_F$ on bidegree $(a,r)$. The complexes $F^\bullet$ and $h^*F^\bullet$ are K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and $J$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-split-perfect-tensor-kinjective]. Thus $C$ and $B$ represent, respectively, $Rh_*E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F^\bullet$ and $Rh_*(E\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}Lh^*F^\bullet)$.

For an $S$-module sheaf $M$ and a retract $P$ of a finite free $R$-module sheaf, let
$$
t_{M,P}:h_*M\otimes_R P\longrightarrow h_*(M\otimes_S h^*P)
$$
be the ordinary adjunct of $\varepsilon_M\otimes1$ after the ordinary pullback-tensor identification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. This identification sends $s\otimes(m\otimes p)$ to $(s\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes p)$, with inverse $(s\otimes m)\otimes(s'\otimes p)\mapsto ss'\otimes(m\otimes p)$. For $P=R^{\oplus N}$, write $q_{M,N}$ for the inverse of the finite-product identification $t_{M,R^{\oplus N}}$ [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits]. Define actual module-sheaf maps
$$
s_{a,r}=(1_A\otimes p_r)\circ q_{I^a,N_r}\circ h_*(1_{I^a}\otimes h^*i_r):
h_*(I^a\otimes_S h^*F^r)\longrightarrow A^a\otimes_R F^r,
$$
where $1_A$ in bidegree $(a,r)$ means $1_{A^a}$. Use the chain map $s:B\to C$ whose degree-$n$ component is $\bigoplus_{a+r=n}s_{a,r}$, under the canonical finite-sum identification
$$
B^n\cong\bigoplus_{a+r=n}h_*(I^a\otimes_S h^*F^r).
$$
These sums are finite because $F^\bullet$ is bounded. The ordinary counit is natural [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. The splitting formulas give $s_{a,r}t_{I^a,F^r}=1$ and $t_{I^a,F^r}s_{a,r}=1$. Consequently, for each module map in either variable, the naturality equation $B(u)t=t'A(u)$ implies $s'B(u)=A(u)s$ by multiplication by the two inverses. Applied to $d_I$ and $d_F$, this specifies compatibility with both differentials; the indices are preserved, so both sides have the same sign $(-1)^a$. Define $\rho_{h,E,F}$ to be the image of this finite-total chain map $s$ in $D(R)$, under the displayed identifications of $B$ and $C$. Its degreewise construction is the displayed $\rho_{F^r}$ formula. This is the precise meaning of bounded totalization of those term maps.

split_report.summary: Second reading repairs the under-specified totalization by constructing actual module-sheaf maps on a K-injective representative, citing existing K-flat, K-injective and derived-adjunction results. Removed the new representative lemma: its inverse-totalization clause repeats the downstream theorem, and its derived representatives were unspecified. The finite-free and retract formulas are retained, with coefficient rings explicit and differential compatibility written out. No new nodes. Maintainer reading adds the existing underived ringed-topos module tensor comparison as an explicit statement dependency; the derived comparison statement alone does not provide that underived isomorphism.
split_report.blueprint: Definition order 1264: adjoint arrow, finite-free inverse, projective splitting formula, bounded totalization. The last sentence is expanded using the actual term maps described in paragraphs 1–2 of the proof of blueprint lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-totalization, without citing that downstream node or using its derived inverse conclusion.
